proposed_widenings.name: CastingTime.hours
proposed_widenings.justification: Hallow has a 24-hour casting time. Current CastingTime supports action, bonus_action, reaction, and minutes. No hours variant exists.

proposed_widenings.name: Duration.permanent
proposed_widenings.justification: Hallow's duration is permanent until dispelled. No existing Duration variant covers this — instantaneous, concentration, and timed all have finite lifespans or require active maintenance. Dispel is the only termination path.

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation: area_entry_block
proposed_widenings.justification: Hallowed Ward prevents creatures of a chosen type from willingly entering the area. This is mechanically distinct from roll_modifier and damage_on_hit — it is a continuous spatial barrier keyed to creature type. The v4 atom block_travel exists but has no surface OngoingOperation variant for area-entry-by-type-filter.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Creatures of the chosen types can't willingly enter the area

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation: condition_suppress_in_area
proposed_widenings.justification: Hallowed Ward suppresses possession, Charmed, and Frightened conditions inflicted by the warded creature types on creatures inside the area. This is an ongoing passive condition-suppression effect scoped to an area — not representable as roll_modifier or damage_on_hit.
proposed_widenings.evidence: any creature that is possessed by or that has the Charmed or Frightened condition from such creatures isn't possessed, Charmed, or Frightened by them while in the area

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation: area_passive_rider (resistance, vulnerability, condition, block_teleport, environment)
proposed_widenings.justification: The 10 Extra Effect options include granting resistance, vulnerability, applying or preventing conditions (Frightened), blocking teleportation/interplanar travel, creating darkness/daylight, silence, and language effects. None of these map to roll_modifier or damage_on_hit. They are area-scoped passive effects that activate while creatures are within the hallowed area.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Resistance: creatures have Resistance to one damage type; Fear: creatures have the Frightened condition; Extradimensional Interference: creatures can't enter or exit using teleportation or interplanar travel; Darkness/Daylight/Silence

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingEffectMechanics.operations as ReadonlyArray<OngoingOperation>
proposed_widenings.justification: Hallow applies two simultaneous ongoing effects: Hallowed Ward (always) plus the chosen Extra Effect. The current OngoingEffectMechanics has a single operation field. This needs to become an array — or a separate multi-operation family is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The affected area has the following effects: [Hallowed Ward — always active] + [one Extra Effect chosen from 10 at cast time]

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation: choice_at_cast (choose one of N options)
proposed_widenings.justification: The Extra Effect is selected by the caster from 10 options at cast time. This is a choose procedure (v4 atom exists) applied at cast time, but there is no surface encoding for 'choose one of these operation variants at cast time and bind it permanently.'
proposed_widenings.evidence: You bind an extra effect to the area from the list below: [Courage, Darkness, Daylight, Peaceful Rest, Extradimensional Interference, Fear, Resistance, Silence, Tongues, Vulnerability]

notes: Hallow fits the ongoing_effect family conceptually — it is a persistent area effect that applies passive riders to creatures within range. However, encoding is blocked by at least four distinct surface gaps: (1) no hours CastingTime variant, (2) no permanent Duration variant, (3) no area-passive OngoingOperation variants (entry-block, condition-suppress, resistance, vulnerability, etc.), and (4) single-operation constraint on OngoingEffectMechanics prevents Hallowed Ward + Extra Effect coexistence. The choose-at-cast mechanic for the Extra Effect is an additional surface gap. All proposed widenings use existing v4 atoms (block_travel, apply_condition, remove_condition, grant_resistance, etc.) — no new v4 atoms are needed, only new surface variants to expose them.
